name: Vermont

agency.name: Vermont Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Program

rates2026.note: Indexed every January 1 (CPI-U or 5%, whichever is smaller)

tipped.note: Service or tipped employees of hotels, motels, tourist places and restaurants who customarily receive more than $120 a month in tips: one-half the minimum wage

source.quote: Effective 01/01/2026: $14.42 per hour worked/ $7.21 for tipped employees

overtime.note: Time and a half after 40 hours a week, but the state rule excludes employees of retail or service establishments, hotels, motels and restaurants, seasonal amusement establishments and some others (the federal FLSA may still apply to them).

source.quote: an employer shall not pay an employee less than one and one-half times the regular wage rate for any work done by the employee in excess of 40 hours during a workweek

sickLeave.capNote: Employer may cap accrual at 40 hours in a 12-month period; may impose a waiting period of up to one year before use for new hires.
sickLeave.employerThreshold: all employers; covers employees working an average of at least 18 hours a week (seasonal jobs of 20 weeks or fewer excluded)
sickLeave.note: Paid at the greater of the employee's normal hourly rate or the minimum wage.

source.quote: An employee shall accrue not less than one hour of earned sick time for every 52 hours worked.

familyLeave.stateUnpaidLaw: Vermont Parental and Family Leave Act (expanded by Act 32 of 2025): up to 12 weeks of unpaid job-protected leave in 12 months; parental, bereavement, safe and qualifying exigency leave at employers with 10+ employees, family leave at employers with 15+ employees (employees averaging 30+ hours a week for 12 months).

source.quote: Eligible employees can take up to 12 weeks of leave in a 12-month period, except as noted otherwise under bereavement leave.

finalPay.quit: on the last regular payday, or the following Friday if there is no regular payday
finalPay.ptoNote: No Vermont statute found requiring payout of accrued vacation; follows employer policy or contract.

source.quote: (1) voluntarily leaves employment shall be paid on the last regular pay day, or if there is no regular pay day, on the following Friday; (2) is discharged from employment shall be paid within 72 hours of discharge

breaks.meal: reasonable opportunities during work periods to eat (no fixed length or timing)
breaks.rest: reasonable opportunities to use toilet facilities

source.quote: An employer shall provide an employee with reasonable opportunities during work periods to eat and to use toilet facilities

notes.text: Act 32 of 2025 widened unpaid leave: bereavement leave (up to 2 weeks, within one year of the death), safe leave and qualifying exigency leave, and a broader definition of family member.

source.quote: Leave is limited to 2 weeks (10 workdays), no more than 5 days taken consecutively, and must be taken within 1 year of the death.

notes.text: Hotels, motels, restaurants and retail or service establishments are excluded from Vermont's overtime rule.

source.quote: (3) Employees of an establishment that is a hotel, motel, or restaurant.

uncertain: 2027 minimum wage: by statute it is indexed on January 1, 2027 (CPI to Sept 1, 2026, max 5%), but no official 2027 figure was found: labor.vermont.gov/newsroom returns 403 and no 2027 poster/press release URL exists. rates2027 left empty.

Vermont Family and Medical Leave Insurance (FMLI, voluntary program for private employers and individuals, run with The Hartford) could not be verified: no official page reachable (fmli.vermont.gov does not resolve, web search unavailable). paidProgram set to false because there is no mandatory state program; the voluntary FMLI should be added once verified.
PTO payout: no statute requiring payout found, but no official page stating 'policy' was read; ptoSource null.
